author: sjm41
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
IPR001282 Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel G6pdl (Q9VNW4)

* **Description of issue**
IPR001282 is currently annotated with the (relatively high level) MF term "[oxidoreductase activity, acting on CH-OH group of donors (GO:0016614)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0016614)". (also see https://github.com/geneontology/go-annotation/issues/2121)
However, this signature is also found in the pseudo enzyme Dmel G6pdl (Q9VNW4), which lacks catalytic activity, so I think the GO term should be removed.

Note: Dmel G6pdl (Q9VNW4) is a paralog of G6pd (P12646) - while both proteins have IPR001282, only G6pd has IPR019796 Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase, active site, from where it correctly gets annotated with [glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase activity (GO:0004345)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0004345)
title: InterPro2GO issue: IPR001282 Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase

author: sarach06
body:
Dear Steven,
Thank you very much for this. Yes, you are right, I removed GO:0016614 from this entry. This will be visible in InterPro 111.0.

Best wishes,
Sara
